No-show fee

I was there.

This is a provisional ruling made by an automated system.

Ruling

Fee stands, driver compensated DRIVER_COMPENSATION

The fee stands. The driver is paid SGD 3.60. No refund.

The judge's explanation, as written

To the rider: the $4.50 no-show cancellation fee stands, and no part of it is refunded. To the driver: you are paid $3.60 compensation (80% of the $4.50 fee in force); the remaining 20% is the platform's service fee. Why the fee stands — POL-NS-01 needs all four limbs, and all four hold. (a) The trip record EV-TRIP-02736 carries a driver 'arrived' event at 13:24:34. (b) The GPS trace EV-GPS-02736 places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from that moment — the longest qualifying in-geofence run starts at 13:24:34 and runs 44 qualifying fixes. (c) The in-geofence dwell, measured from the first qualifying fix and not from the arrival tap, is 428 s, comfortably over the 180 s free waiting period in force (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180; no_show_threshold_sec is not set, so no longer threshold applies). (d) No boarding occurred and the driver terminated the trip at 13:31:43 under RIDER_NO_SHOW, one second after the dwell elapsed. Nothing displaces the fee. POL-NS-03 does not apply: the driver's stationary fixes were inside the arrival radius, not at a wrong face of the venue. POL-NS-05 does not apply: the arrival marker was not false — the recomputed clock begins at the first qualifying in-geofence fix, which is the tapped moment itself (dwell start offset 0.0 s), so there is no false-arrival referral. POL-NS-06 gives no refund: the dwell exceeds the 180 s minimum by 248 s, so there is no shortfall, and the missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02736-01 (weight 0.0) is irrelevant because no separate in-geofence intervals need to be summed. POL-NS-10 refunds nothing: the rider did not cancel and no waiting-time fee was charged (waiting_time_fee 0.00). The rider's claim 'I was there.' does not change this. The only route by which a rider's presence or coordination defeats a no-show fee is POL-NS-04, and it fails at its first limb: the chat log EV-CHAT-02736 holds exactly one message and it is the driver's ('hi im at the pickup point', 13:24:59), so no rider locating or coordinating message exists on the record. POL-NS-04 therefore does not exonerate the rider and the fee is untouched. (Claims built on the rider device track were discarded before me for failure to disclose the GPS impairment and are not relied on here.) Driver compensation — POL-NS-07 pays 80% of the $4.50 fee in force = $3.60 (the figure the fare ledger also computes). The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the '4 or more' limb, and 2 divided by 64 completed trips in 30 days is 0.03, below the 0.08 limb. Compensation is therefore paid, and under POL-GEN-03 the ruling value is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd mirroring the $3.60 — the charge to the rider stands as it presently is (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). The fee line reconciles to the fee in force ($4.50 = $4.50 net), so no POL-NS-08(d) integrity defect arises. Weight and confidence. The finding rests on the driver's in-geofence arrival and dwell, and only the GPS trace EV-GPS-02736 carries that fact. That artifact is impaired at weight 0.85 with issue code GPS_GAP_SHORT_OR_OUTSIDE_WINDOW — a 60 s sampling gap from 13:21:14 to 13:22:14. The gap lies before the waiting window opened and is under POL-NS-08(b)'s 120 s policy threshold, so it does not impair the arrival or dwell finding and the finding survives the discount; under POL-GEN-02(2), however, it caps confidence at 0.85. The trip record, chat log and fare breakdown are each at weight 1.0, and no independent artifact carries the in-geofence position fact, so the cap remains 0.85. That is above the 0.70 floor, so the case does not escalate. No POL-NS-09 trigger fires: no two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence; there is no repeat-dispute pattern between these parties; the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip; and no deciding fact rests solely on an artifact impaired under POL-NS-08(a)–(d). The monetary effect ($3.60) is below the $8.00 execution threshold, so this provisional ruling executes automatically. Both parties may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04. The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

How to appeal: Either party may appeal once within 30 days. A different human reviewer hears it, and only record evidence may be added.

Read POL-GEN-04 in full
Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

confidence 0.85floor 0.7 (POL-GEN-02)

POL-GEN-05: the monetary effect is SGD 3.60 against an execution threshold of SGD 8.00. It does not exceed the threshold, so the amount is executed automatically on issue, subject to POL-GEN-04.
